facts.statement: Coelacanthus was the first genus of coelacanths to be described, occurring roughly a century before the living coelacanth Latimeria was discovered.
facts.quote: It was the first genus of coelacanths described, about a century before the discovery of the extant coelacanth Latimeria.

facts.statement: The order Coelacanthiformes is named after the extinct genus Coelacanthus.
facts.quote: It was the first genus of coelacanths described, about a century before the discovery of the extant coelacanth Latimeria. The order Coelacanthiformes is named after it.

facts.statement: Individuals of Coelacanthus grew up to 0.7 meters in length and possessed small lobed fins, suggesting they were open-water predators.
facts.quote: Individuals grew up to 0.7 m in length, had an elongate codavypter or supplementary tail lobe, and had small lobed fins, suggesting that Coelacanthus were open-water predators.

facts.statement: The hollow fin rays of the caudal fin gave Coelacanthus its name.
facts.quote: The fin rays of the caudal fin are hollow, which gave Coelacanthus its name.

facts.statement: Coelacanthus is an extinct genus of coelacanths that originally appeared during the Permian period.
facts.quote: Coelacanthus, del griego clásico κοῖλος (koîlos), "hueco", y ἄκανθος (ákanthos), "espina", es un género extinto de celacantos que aparecieron originalmente durante el período Pérmico.

facts.statement: Coelacanthus survived the Permian-Triassic mass extinction and went extinct sometime during the Late Jurassic, approximately 145 million years ago.
facts.quote: Coelacanthus fue un género longevo con una distribución cosmopolita. Logró sobrevivir la extinción masiva del Pérmico-Triásico, y se extinguió en algún momento durante el final del período Jurásico Superior, hace cerca de 145 millones de años.

facts.statement: Members of this genus had a superficial resemblance to the modern coelacanth Latimeria, though they were smaller and had more elongated heads.
facts.quote: Los miembros de este género tenían un parecido superficial al actual celacanto Latimeria, aunque eran más pequeños, y tenían cabezas más alargadas.

facts.statement: The genus Coelacanthus was established by Agassiz in 1836.
The genus Coelacanthus was named by Agassiz in 1839 according to the Paleobiology Database.
The only definitive species in the genus is C. granulatus, found in the late Permian Kupferschiefer of Germany and equivalent Marl Slate of England.
facts.quote: The only definitive species in this genus is C. granulatus from the late Permian (Wuchiapingian stage) Kupferschiefer of Germany and equivalent Marl Slate of England.

rejected.statement: Coelacanthus bore a superficial similarity to the living coelacanth Latimeria, but was smaller and had a more elongated head.
rejected.quote: Coelacanthus bears a superficial similarity to the living coelacanth Latimeria, though it was smaller, and had a more elongated head.
